16. A similarly high status is granted to Understanding in all the <term>Hermetic Scriptures<gloss>Sacred writings attributed to Hermes Trismegistus, a legendary Hellenistic figure who represents the combination of the Greek god Hermes and the Egyptian god Thoth; these texts form the basis of Western alchemy and esotericism.</gloss></term>. For—as seen in the Book of Isaiah, chapter 11, verse 2—it is always ranked second among the seven <term>Divine Powers<gloss>original: "Elohim"; the Hebrew plural noun for God, interpreted here as the seven spirits or qualities of the Divine.</gloss></term> of God. The first place is assigned to Wisdom, which is considered to be one and the same as Love. This same order is found in the layout of the solar system: for Mercury is Hermes, and his planet is the one closest to the Sun. 

The description in ancient myths of this god having a "thievish disposition," and the legends that portray him as the patron of thieves and adventurers who steals from all the other Gods in turn, are actually ways of describing how easily the faculty of Understanding gathers everything together and makes it its own. Hermes represents that divine part of a human being which searches for and extracts meaning from every area of existence, stepping into the territory of every "God" and taking a portion of their specialized treasures. <note>In Greek mythology, the infant Hermes famously stole the cattle of Apollo; the author interprets this not as a crime, but as the intellect's ability to take knowledge from different fields and synthesize it into understanding.</note> 

In this way, Understanding has a finger on all things and adapts them for its own use, whether it be the "arrows" (rays of truth) of Apollo, the "girdle" (the power of beauty) of Aphrodite, the "oxen" (earthly labor) of Admetus, the "trident" (authority over the subconscious) of Poseidon, or the "tongs" (the tools of creation) of Hephaistos. Not only is Hermes—as previously mentioned—the "rock" upon which the true Church is built <note>The author is making a wordplay on the name "Peter" (from the Greek "Petros," meaning rock), suggesting that the biblical Peter represents the faculty of Understanding rather than a historical person.</note>; he is also the divinity who directly controls all divine revelations and all divine tasks. 

To him belong the rod of knowledge used to measure all things, the wings of courage, the sword of an unbeatable will, and the cap of concealment or discretion. He is, in turn, the Star of the East that leads the <term>Wise Men<gloss>original: "Magi"; the priestly astrologers from the East who sought the Christ-child.</gloss></term>; the Cloud from which the holy Voice speaks; by day the pillar of Smoke, and by night the shining Flame, leading the chosen soul on her dangerous path through the foul <note>original: "noisome"</note> wilderness of the world, as she flees from the...

The Materialist knows not perfection, nor reality, nor **Spirit**, nor **God**; and, knowing none of these, he knows not enthusiasm. Now, not to know enthusiasm, is not to know love. 39. Not always did Materialists contemn enthusiasm and repudiate its products. Of one, at least, history tells who with enthusiasm sang of enthusiasm as the energising force of genius. ## PART V.

47. We come to that which, both in its nature and in its import, is the most stupendous fact of mystical experience, and the crowning experience of seers in all ages from the remotest antiquity to the present day. This is the **Vision of the Lord** <note>original: "Adonai"; a Hebrew name for God, here signifying the manifest personification of the Divine within the soul</note>, a vision which proves that not only subjectively but objectively, not only mentally and theoretically, but sensibly and actually, God, as the Lord, is present and cognisable in each individual, ever operating to build him up in the **Divine Image**, and succeeding so far—and only so far—as the individual, by making the

so is the expression or countenance of man the express image of God's nature, and bears in its features the impress of the celestial, showing him to be thence derived. Thus, in the human face, by the straight, central, protruding, and vertical line of the <term>organ of respiration</term> <note>the nose</note>, is denoted Individuality, the divine Ego, the **I AM**, of the man. Although single exteriorly, and constituting one organ, in token of the **Divine Unity**, within it is dual, having a double function, and two nostrils in which resides the power of the Breath or Spirit, and which represent the **Divine Duality**. This duality finds its especial symbolisation in the two spheres of the eyes, which—placed on a level with the summit of the nose—denote respectively Intelligence and Love, or Father and Mother, as the supreme elements of Being. Although exteriorly two, interiorly they are one, as vision is one. And of the harmonious co-operation of the two personalities represented by them, proceeds, as child, a third personality, which is their joint expression or "**Word**" <note>original: "Logos"</note>. Of this the Mouth is at once the organ and symbol, being in itself dual—when closed a line, when open a circle; and also twofold, being compounded of line and circle in the tongue and lips. And as the place of issue of the creative breath, it is below the other features, since creation, in coming from the Highest, is in its direction necessarily downwards. Thus, in the countenance of the "Image of God," is expressed the nature of God—even the **Holy Trinity**. For "these three are one," being essential modes of the same Being.

50. Enshrined in this light is a Form radiant and glorious beyond all power of expression. From the right hand upraised in attitude indicative of will and command, proceeds, as a stream of living force, the Holy Life and Substance whereby and whereof Creation consists. With the left hand, depressed and open as in attitude of recall, the stream is indrawn, and Creation is sustained and redeemed. Thus projecting and recalling, expanding and contracting, Adonai fulfils the functions expressed in the mystical formula ***Dissolve and Coagulate*** <note>original: "Solve et Coagula"; an alchemical maxim describing the two-fold process of breaking down a substance into its elements and then refining it into a new, higher form</note>. 53. This discourse and series of discourses will fitly close with an exposition of the relations subsisting between the <term>Adonai</term> <note>Hebrew: "The Lord"; the personified, visible aspect of the Divine</note>, the <term>Christ</term>, and the **Man**.
As <term>Adonai</term> the Lord is the manifestation of God in **Substance**, so <term>Christ</term> is the manifestation of the Lord in **Humanity**. The former occurs by **Generation** <note>The process of being brought into physical or substantial existence</note>; the latter by **Regeneration** <note>The process of spiritual rebirth or rising into a higher state of being</note>. The former is from within, outwards; the latter is from below, upwards. **Man**, ascending by evolution from the material and lowermost stratum of existence, finds his highest development in the <term>Christ</term>. This is the point where the human stream, as it flows upwards into God, culminates. Reaching this point by regeneration, man is at once Son of Man and of God, and is perfect, receiving in consequence the baptism of the <term>Logos</term> <note>Greek: "The Word" or "Divine Reason"; the creative principle of God</note> or **Word**, <term>Adonai</term>. # No. IV.

## CONCERNING THE NATURE OF SIN.

*1. As is the Outer so is the Inner: He that worketh is One.* <note>This is a variation of the famous Hermetic axiom "As above, so below," suggesting that the laws of the physical world mirror the laws of the spiritual world.</note>

*2. As the small is, so is the great: there is one Law.*

*3. Nothing is small, and nothing is great in the Divine <term>Economy</term>.* <note>In this context, "Economy" refers to the management and organization of the created universe by God.</note>

*4. If thou wouldst understand the method of the world's corruption, and the condition to which Sin hath reduced the work of God,*

*5. Meditate upon the aspect of a <term>Corpse</term>; and consider the method of the putrefaction of its tissues and humours.* <note>The author uses the visceral image of a decaying body to illustrate how sin acts as a form of spiritual "rot" that breaks down the unity of a being.</note>

*6. For the secret of <term>Death</term> is the same, whether of the Outer or of the Inner.*

### No. V.

## ON THE “GREAT WORK,” REDEMPTION, AND THE ROLE OF CHRIST JESUS WITHIN IT.

*“**F**OR this cause is Christ manifest, that he may destroy the works of the devil.”* <note>This quote from the First Epistle of John (3:8) is used here to define "the devil" not as a person, but as the "works" of material attachment and illusion that keep the spirit imprisoned.</note>

*2. In this passage of the holy writings is contained the explanation of the mission of the Christ, and the nature of the Great Work.* <note>The "Great Work" (often referred to in Latin as the <term>Magnum Opus</term>) is a central concept in alchemy and mysticism, signifying the process of purifying the human soul into a divine state.</note>

*3. The Great Work is the redemption of Spirit from Matter; that is, the establishment of the Kingdom of God.*

*4. Jesus being asked when the Kingdom of God should come, answered, “When Two shall be as One, and that which is Without as that which is Within.”* <note>This saying is not found in the standard New Testament but appears in early Christian texts like the Gospel of Thomas and the Gospel of the Egyptians. It describes a state of non-duality where the physical and spiritual are no longer in conflict.</note>

*5. In saying this, he expressed the nature of the Great Work. The Two are Spirit and Matter: the Within is the Real Invisible; the Without is the Illusory Visible.* <note>The "Real Invisible" refers to the eternal world of the soul and God, while the "Illusory Visible" refers to the physical world, which is seen as a temporary projection or shadow.</note>

*6. The Kingdom of God shall come when Spirit and Matter shall be one Substance, and the Phenomenal shall be absorbed into the Real.* <note>The "Phenomenal" refers to the world of appearances—things we perceive with our five senses—which the mystic believes must eventually return to its spiritual source.</note>

*7. His design was therefore to destroy the dominion of Matter, and to dissipate the “devil” and his works.*

*8. And this he intended to accomplish by proclaiming the knowledge of the Universal Dissolvent, and giving to men the keys of the Kingdom of God.* <note>In alchemy, the "Universal Dissolvent" (<term>Alkahest</term>) is a substance that can dissolve all solids. In this spiritual context, it represents the Divine Spirit or Love that "dissolves" the hardened ego and material attachments.</note>

*9. Now, the Kingdom of God is within us; that is, it is interior, invisible, Mystic, Spiritual.*

*10. There is a power by means of which the Outer may be absorbed into the Inner.*

<summary>This page defines the "Great Work" as the alchemical and spiritual process of reuniting matter with spirit. It frames Christ's mission as providing the "Universal Dissolvent" necessary to break down the illusions of the physical world and establish the internal Kingdom of God.</summary>

## No. VI.

### THE TIME OF THE END.

*As there was a return of the Spirit or Angel of <note>Elias is the Latin form of the name Elijah. In Christian tradition, John the Baptist is seen as the return of Elijah's spirit.</note>Elias in the person of John the Baptist before the advent of Jesus, so there will be a return of the Angel of Daniel before the next manifestation of the Christ. Daniel’s Angel is he who specially foretold the culmination, and hour of overthrow, of the world’s materialistic system in Church, State, and Society. And when he had completed his prediction he told Daniel that he — Daniel — should rest for the present, but when the accomplished time was come, and the “End” was at hand, he should return and stand again and prophesy before the world. A like assurance was given also to John. And the token whereby the approach of the End should be known, would be the spectacle of “the <note>This phrase refers to a prophecy in the Book of Daniel and the Gospels, traditionally interpreted as a desecration of the Temple, but here interpreted as a spiritual state.</note>Abomination of Desolation standing in the holy place.” Now the “holy place” is always — whether in the individual or the universal, the <term>Macrocosm</term> or the <term>Microcosm</term> — the place of God and the Soul. And “the Abomination of Desolation” — or “that maketh desolate” — is that system of thought which, putting Matter in the chief place, and making it the Source, Substance, and Object of Existence, abolishes God out of the Universe and the Soul out of Man, and thus, depriving Existence of its Light and Life, makes it empty, desolate, and barren, a very abomination of desolation.*

<note>The author argues that "Materialism"—the belief that only physical matter exists—is the true "Abomination" because it empties the human experience of spiritual meaning, effectively "desolating" the soul which should be the dwelling place of the Divine.</note>

<summary>This passage interprets biblical prophecy through a mystical lens, identifying the "Abomination of Desolation" as the rise of modern materialism which denies the existence of the soul.</summary>

## No. VIII.

### CONCERNING THE BOOK OF ESTHER.

*ONE of the most mystic books in the Old Testament, and the most nearly about to be fulfilled, is the book of Esther.*

*This book is a prophecy, written in the form of an actual history.*

*The Great King Assuerus <note>Original Latin form of the name Ahasuerus, the Persian king usually identified as Xerxes I.</note>, who had all the world under his dominion, and possessed the wealth of all the nations, is the Genius of the Age <note>A term referring to the "Zeitgeist" or the dominant intellectual and worldly spirit that governs a particular period of history.</note>.*

*Queen Vashti, who for her disobedience to the king was deposed from her royal seat, is the Orthodox Catholic Church <note>In this mystical context, Vashti represents established, institutional religion which loses its influence when it fails to serve the "King" or the divine purpose.</note>.*

*The Jews, scattered among the nations under the dominion of the king, are the true Israel of God <note>A term used here to describe the spiritually enlightened or the "elect" who remain faithful to divine truth regardless of their physical location.</note>.*

*Mardochi <note>The Latin form of the name Mordecai.</note> the Jew represents the spirit of intuitive Reason and Understanding.*

*His enemy Aman <note>The Latin form of the name Haman.</note>, is the spirit of Materialism, taken into the favour and protection of the Genius of the Age, and exalted to the highest place in the world's councils after the deposition of the orthodox religion.*

*Now Aman has a wife and ten sons.*

*Esther, who, under the care and tuition of Mardochi, is brought up pure and virgin, is that spirit of love and sympathetic interpretation which shall redeem the world.*

*I have told you that it shall be redeemed by a "woman."*

<summary>This page presents an esoteric, allegorical reading of the Book of Esther, where the historical figures represent competing spiritual and worldly forces like Materialism, Intuition, and the Spirit of the Age. It identifies Esther as the "feminine" spirit of love and interpretation destined to save the world from the dominance of materialistic thought.</summary>

# THE PERFECT WAY.

*Now the several philosophical systems by which the Councillors of the Age propose to replace the dethroned Church, are one by one submitted to the judgment of the Age; and Esther, coming last, shall find favour.*

*Six years shall she be anointed with oil of Myrrh <note>In mystical traditions, myrrh often represents the bitterness of discipline, asceticism, and the intellectual rigor required to purify the mind.</note>, that is, with study and training severe and bitter, that she may be proficient in intellectual knowledge, as must all systems which seek the favour of the Age.*

*And six years with sweet perfumes, that is with the gracious loveliness of the imagery and poetry of the Faiths of the Past, that Religion may not be lacking in sweetness and beauty.*

*But she shall not seek to put on any of those adornments of dogma, or of mere sense, which, by trick of priestcraft, former systems have used to gain power or favour with the world and the Age, and for which they have been found wanting.*

*Now there come out of the darkness and the storm which shall arise upon the earth, two Dragons <note>These "Dragons" likely symbolize the conflicting forces of the time—perhaps absolute materialism and fanatical superstition—which battle for dominance in the absence of true spiritual light.</note>.*

*And they fight and tear each other, until there arises a Star, a Fountain of Light, a Queen, who is Esther.*

*This is the key. Unlock the meaning of all that is written.*

*I have told you that which shall be in the days about to come.*

## Fig. 7. The Cherubim (Ezekiel and <term>Apocalypse (the Book of Revelation)</term>) representing,—

**1st.** The Elemental Spirits of the <term>Macrocosm (the great world or universe)</term> and <term>Microcosm (the little world of the human being)</term>.

## Fig. 10. The Tabernacle in the Wilderness. <note>The portable sanctuary used by the Israelites during their desert wanderings, interpreted here as a map of the soul or a symbolic representation of the spiritual journey toward the Divine.</note>

**1.** Open Court.
**2.** Holy Place—the Tent, or Covered House.
**3.** Holy of Holies. <note>The innermost sanctum of the Tabernacle, representing the most sacred space where the Divine presence resided and where only the High Priest could enter once a year.</note>
**A.** Altar of Oblations. <term>Oblations (sacred offerings or sacrifices brought to God)</term>
**B.** Censer. <note>A vessel used for burning incense during ritual worship, symbolizing prayers rising to heaven.</note>
**C.** Laver. <note>A large basin containing water for the priests to wash themselves before performing rituals to signify spiritual purification.</note>
**D.** Altar of Incense.
**E.** Golden Candlestick. <note>The seven-branched lampstand, or Menorah, symbolizing divine light and the seven days of creation.</note>
**F.** Table of Shewbread. <note>A table holding twelve loaves of "bread of the presence," symbolizing the twelve tribes of Israel and God's provision.</note>
**G.** Veil dividing the Tent or Covered House into two parts.
**H.** Ark of the Covenant containing the Rod, the <term>Host (the jar of Manna)</term>, and the Law. <note>The Ark was the most sacred object in the Tabernacle, housing the stone tablets of the Ten Commandments (the Law), Aaron's rod that budded, and a golden jar of manna, the miraculous food provided by God in the desert.</note>
